Since both benign and malignant tumors can have large sizes, this geometric dependency is not clinically meaningful and leads to misclassification of benign cases as malignant.

result.explanation: Both misclassified samples (541 and 340) exhibit high mean radius and mean area values, which are strongly correlated with each other due to the geometric relationship between radius and area (area ≈ π × radius²). This leads to a spurious correlation where high mean radius and high mean area appear together, even though they are mathematically linked rather than biologically meaningful in cancer classification. Additionally, both samples show moderate to low values in mean smoothness and mean compactness, which are known to be more relevant to malignancy (malignant tumors typically have irregular shapes and lower smoothness), yet the model incorrectly treats these as indicative of malignancy. However, the shared feature pattern—especially the high radius/area combination—is not biologically significant in diagnosing cancer, as benign tumors can also have large sizes. The model may have learned this geometric correlation as a proxy for malignancy, leading to misclassification. Thus, the shared features represent spurious correlations driven by mathematical dependencies rather than biological or clinical relevance.
